column1: Rinse the rice, soak it for 20–30 minutes, and cook it with the water using your preferred method.
Microwave the seasoning soy sauce and sugar for 30–60 seconds and whisk until the sugar dissolves. Stir in the sesame oil and salt.
Put the hot rice in a large bowl, pour over the seasoning, and fold it in gently with a rice paddle without mashing. Let it cool just enough to handle.
Wet an onigiri mold (or use plastic wrap), pack it with rice, press firmly, and unmold onto parchment. Repeat with the remaining rice to make about 9.
With damp hands, press each rice ball firmly into a tight triangle so it holds together on the pan.
Mix the glaze soy sauce and sesame oil. Line a large frying pan with parchment paper.
Grill the rice balls on the parchment over medium-low heat, turning only once each side has browned, until crisp all over.
Lower the heat, brush the glaze on top and sides, flip to caramelize the glazed side, then brush the other side. Cook until glossy and golden, taking care not to burn, and serve.
